events.title: Allied Landings at Gallipoli
events.description: Australian, New Zealand, British, and French forces landed on the Gallipoli Peninsula in the Ottoman Empire during World War I, aiming to open a sea route to Russia by capturing Constantinople. The campaign bogged down into months of stalemate and ended in Allied withdrawal in January 1916.
events.significance: The date is commemorated as ANZAC Day in Australia and New Zealand, a national day of remembrance that helped shape the national identities of both countries.

events.title: Watson and Crick Publish the Structure of DNA
events.description: James Watson and Francis Crick published their paper in the journal Nature proposing the double-helix structure of DNA, building on X-ray diffraction work by Rosalind Franklin and Maurice Wilkins.
events.significance: The discovery explained how genetic information is stored and replicated, launching the era of modern molecular biology, genetics, and biotechnology.

events.title: Carnation Revolution in Portugal
events.description: A military coup led by the Movement of the Armed Forces overthrew the Estado Novo dictatorship in Lisbon, largely without bloodshed. Civilians placed carnations in soldiers' rifle barrels, giving the revolution its name.
events.significance: It ended nearly 50 years of authoritarian rule, led to democracy in Portugal, and hastened the independence of Portuguese colonies in Africa such as Angola and Mozambique.

events.title: Israel Completes Withdrawal from the Sinai Peninsula
events.description: Israel completed its withdrawal from the Sinai Peninsula, returning the territory to Egypt as required by the 1979 Egypt-Israel Peace Treaty, which followed the Camp David Accords.
events.significance: It was a landmark step in Arab-Israeli peace efforts, demonstrating that land-for-peace agreements could be implemented and solidifying the first peace treaty between Israel and an Arab state.

events.title: Hubble Space Telescope Deployed
events.description: The Hubble Space Telescope was deployed into low Earth orbit from the Space Shuttle Discovery during mission STS-31. After a repair mission in 1993 corrected its flawed primary mirror, it began returning extraordinarily sharp images.
events.significance: Hubble transformed astronomy by helping determine the age of the universe, revealing deep-field galaxies, and providing evidence for the universe's accelerating expansion.
